style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#8c8f98;fontSize=11;fontFamily=IBM Plex Sans;spacing=0;" value="A submit call answers each entry once its row is committed and publishes after the answer, so the job store and not the broker bounds the answer, and the reconciler publishes whatever a call left unpublished. Control writes the request to the job row first: a job that never started is settled on the row alone, and for a started job the retrier delivers cancel, terminate and pause to its workflow while admission delivers resume. Every call is safe to repeat." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="56" width="1070" x="20" y="806" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

127.0.0.1:18081: uploads, batch submit, batch reads

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #c9cbd0;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans'; color: #c9cbd0; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Submit sequence, per chunk of entries
1. validate each entry, derive its job id from its key, fingerprint it
2. index the template's content and link it to each job, commit
3. insert the job rows and one accepted event per row, commit
4. answer one line per entry: accepted, duplicate or rejected
5. publish each new row's accepted event, and on ACCEPTED
set the receipt once and record that it was published

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 367px; margin-left: 213px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #c9cbd0;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans'; color: #c9cbd0; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Reconciler
rows still accepted with no receipt after a grace period:
rebuild the accepted event byte for byte and publish it again

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 464px; margin-left: 213px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #c9cbd0;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans'; color: #c9cbd0; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
control-api listener
127.0.0.1:18080: control of a job or a batch, job status

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 551px; margin-left: 213px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #c9cbd0;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans'; color: #c9cbd0; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Control table
under the row lock, decides from the status, whether a workflow exists
and the outstanding action: applied, requested, noop or refused,
with the row writes and events in one transaction.
A resume is only requested on the row, never signalled

div.div:
Control retrier
sends each outstanding cancel, terminate or pause to its workflow
until the server accepts it, then marks it delivered.
Its resume finisher returns a row whose workflow is gone
to accepted, for admission to start again

div.div: A submit call answers each entry once its row is committed and publishes after the answer, so the job store and not the broker bounds the answer, and the reconciler publishes whatever a call left unpublished. Control writes the request to the job row first: a job that never started is settled on the row alone, and for a started job the retrier delivers cancel, terminate and pause to its workflow while admission delivers resume. Every call is safe to repeat.
